newsitem.title: UK: Major says will not accept "phoney" IRA ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Major says will not accept "phoney" IRA ceasefire.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Sunday he was not prepared to accept a "phoney" IRA ceasefire just to secure the participation of the guerrilla movement's political wing Sinn Fein in Northern Irish peace talks.

Speaking on BBC television ahead of talks on Monday in London with Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, Major said he was not optimistic about the chances of a new Irish Republican Army (IRA) ceasefire, but said he could not rule one out either.
However, he stressed, "I am not interested in a phoney ceasefire."

Major said Britain had previously been betrayed by the IRA which he said had continued to prepare to carry on its violent war to end British rule of Northern Ireland even after it had called a ceasefire in 1994.
That ceasefire came to a violent end in February this year with an IRA bomb in London which killed two people.
This was followed up by an attack in Manchester and most recently by a bomb at a British army base in Northern Ireland in October.
Major said he wanted to see a genuine ceasefire which could be effectively monitored by British intelligence. "This time it needs to be real", Major said.
Once he was convinced that any ceasefire was genuine, he would be as strong an advocate of Sinn Fein participation in peace talks "as the Sinn Fein themselves," Major said.
